newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH OPPOSITION CENTRE PARTY WANTS NO ERM LINK.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH OPPOSITION CENTRE PARTY WANTS NO ERM LINK.

text.p: Finland's opposition Centre Party does not think the markka should be linked to Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM), party chairman Esko Aho said on Thursday.

The party's parliamentary group did not decide formally its stance on a potential ERM-link at a meeting on Thursday, but Aho and group chairman Aapo Saari told a Reuters reporter that the centrists' decision would be made "very soon".
"Now it is not sensible to peg the markka to the exchange rate mechanism so our stance is negative," Aho said.
The party's representatives on the Bank of Finland board of parliamentary supervisor would be advised to vote in line with the group's decision, the centrist leaders said.

The Centre Party has three members on the nine-strong supervisory board, which by law is charged with the task of passing to the government any proposal by the central bank management board to link the markka to ERM.
At least one other supervisory board member, the Leftist Alliance party's single representative, is an outspoken opponent of an ERM-link.

Six of the parliamentary supervisors must be present to make a quorum. The board of supervisors could decide by simple majority in favour or against forwarding an ERM-link proposal to the government, a Bank of Finland spokesman said.
